origins: When money has solved real problems, such as a repair, a medical bill, or a hard season, it is easy to conclude that it can solve everything. Families who handle conflict by paying for it, or who show love with gifts, can pass this lesson on. The belief holds until a problem comes along that money cannot touch, such as grief, a broken trust, loneliness, or a wandering heart.
teaches: Scripture teaches that money is useful but limited. “He who loves money is never satisfied by money.” “Riches are worthless in the day of wrath, but righteousness brings deliverance from death.” Jesus asked, “What does it profit a man to gain the whole world, yet forfeit his soul?” Paul learned to be content in every situation, because his strength came from Christ. God gives wealth for good use, but the deepest problems need what money cannot buy: forgiveness, love, presence, and truth.
self_statements: If I just had enough money, this would be solved.
I can pay my way out of anything.
Problems are only a matter of resources.
Giving gifts shows people I care.
Money is the answer to every worry.
If it cannot be bought, it does not matter.
errors: Turning “money solved this” into “money solves everything.”
Seeing every problem as either solvable with money or hopeless.
Noticing what money has fixed and overlooking what it could not.
Treating money as far more powerful than it is.
questions: What problems have I faced that money could not fix?
What do I feel when money cannot solve a problem?
Is there a relationship or need I have tried to solve with money instead of time and presence?
What does the Bible say about the limits of wealth?
What would it look like to bring this problem to God and to people, not only to my accounts?
What is one thing I need that money cannot buy?
truth: Money is a good tool, but it cannot forgive me, heal my grief, or love me. Some of life’s deepest needs are met only by God and by people. I can use my resources wisely and also turn to what money can never provide.
hw_truths: Money is a tool, not a savior.
Some problems need presence, not payment.
God provides what money cannot buy.
I can use money wisely and trust God.
I can be content in many situations.
Time and love are worth more than gifts.
log: What money could and could not do
Each week, write one problem that money helped and one that it could not touch, and what helped that one.
actions: Make two lists: problems money can help and problems it cannot. Notice what is on the second list.
Spend an hour with someone this week with no gift attached.
Bring one money-proof problem to God.
Pray specifically about a problem that cannot be bought off.
Name three things that are enough today.
prayer: Lord, thank You for what You provide. Keep me from trusting in money to save me. Help me turn to You and to people for what money cannot buy, and teach me to be content in You. Amen.
hw_questions: What problem have I tried to solve with money that needs something else?
What can money never buy for me?
What would presence look like instead of payment?
Where do I need to trust God more than my resources?
Who needs my time more than my gift?
name_example: Sarah can write: “Money is useful, but my deepest needs are met by God and by people.”
meta: Christian belief counseling for “Money can fix any problem.” with BSB scriptures, questions, songs, and practical homework.
